breaking.headline: Stocks set to surge on Black Friday as AI shares rebound
breaking.fact: S&P 500 futures were up about 1.7% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 2.5% early Friday, with Nvidia up 4.7% and AMD up 7% premarket, after global markets rallied Thursday on relief that Trump's new tariffs look manageable; Wall Street reopens for a shortened session, closing at 1 PM ET.

breaking.headline: Trump fires new tariff salvo at 14 partners; allies' levies look capped
breaking.fact: Trump on Wednesday proposed new Section 301 tariffs of 20% to 40% on 14 trading partners including China, Japan and the EU over excess industrial capacity, but the USTR said it will cap new levies at levels agreed under trade deals — the EU's 15% cap holds and nothing takes effect before February or March 2027 — and global markets rallied Thursday as the hit looked manageable.

breaking.headline: Second judge blocks Trump's birthright citizenship order
breaking.fact: US District Judge Christopher Cooper in Washington on Wednesday blocked enforcement of Trump's August executive order curtailing birthright citizenship, in a class action for children who would be denied citizenship; a Maryland judge blocked it in September, so the administration must overturn both rulings to enforce it.

breaking.headline: CDC reports nine measles deaths in worst US outbreak in decades
breaking.fact: The CDC reported nine measles-related deaths in the US this year and 6,039 confirmed cases as of Nov 24 across 47 jurisdictions, the worst outbreak in decades; the agency said the death count could change as it reviews more state reports, and publicly reported state figures already point to at least 14 deaths.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed Thursday in Paris at €190.32, up 1.0%, as the CAC 40 jumped 1.8% while Wall Street was dark for Thanksgiving. At the ECB's Nov 26 reference rate of 1.0975 the quote converts to $208.88, not far from the year's high of €194.70. Steady European industrial-gas demand is doing the work, and Friday's Paris session will set the next print as U.S. futures point to a rebound.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic ended Wednesday at $82.79, up 1.1%, holding just under its $83 IPO price as the AI selloff paused for the holiday. The math world is still waiting on its Nov 20 Navier-Stokes blow-up claim with NYU's Tristan Buckmaster, whose numerical certificate has yet to be released, so the proof stays unverified. With AI names rebounding premarket Friday, the stock gets its next read in the half session.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: The Treasury-bill fund ticked up a penny Wednesday to $91.64, doing what it is built for while the Nasdaq plunged 4.6% intraday and the VIX spiked to 28.29. Its distribution yield is 4.04%, on a $0.30849-per-share payout made Nov 5. With a December hike priced as near-certain and futures pointing to a Friday rebound, BIL's quiet steadiness stays the point as growth stocks whipsaw.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet gave back 2.1% Wednesday to close at $273.10, caught in the chip-led selloff as the Nasdaq slid 0.6% and hot PCE data pushed December hike odds toward 95%. There was no Alphabet-specific news behind the drop — it was the rate-sensitive growth trade unwinding. Google's research arm posted six AI math papers Nov 25, and futures point to a tech rebound in Friday's half session.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly eased 1.1% Wednesday to $1,392.22, giving back part of Tuesday's 3.2% jump as money rotated into defensive names and out of growth. The pullback was modest next to the Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge, and Lilly held up well through the afternoon recovery. With futures pointing higher into Friday's half session, the drugmaker's next move waits on whether the safety trade holds.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 2.0% Wednesday to $301.99 while the broader market fell apart intraday, and the energy backdrop only strengthened since. Brent is near $97.30 and WTI $85.85 on Friday as Gulf shipping attacks and a Houthi strike on a Saudi refinery keep supply fears high. Tight global gas markets and rising Gulf tensions keep favoring U.S. LNG exporters, and the run looks durable.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia dropped 3.9% Wednesday to $149.30, giving back more of Monday's 31% surge after Huang returned, and S&P put its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative on governance grounds. The FT reported Nvidia halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations under new U.S. export rules, pending Washington guidance. The stock is up 4.7% premarket Friday as AI names rebound into the half session.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer finished flat Wednesday at $28.46, keeping Tuesday's 3.9% gain as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers during the market's wild intraday swing. The drugmaker's calm stood out while the Nasdaq plunged 4.6% before recovering and the VIX spiked to 28.29. With futures pointing higher Friday, Pfizer's dividend yield keeps it on the safe-haven list heading into the half session.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab bounced 2.3% Wednesday to $47.02, riding the market's late-day recovery after Tuesday's 7.4% slide. The space stock is one of the tape's most volatile names, swinging hard with risk appetite as the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before clawing most of it back. No company news drove the move — pure sentiment — so Friday's thin half session could bring another sharp swing either way.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital gained 2.9% Wednesday to $8.92, extending a strong week as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield pulled in buyers during the market's flight to income. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.85% as stocks recovered from their intraday lows, a friendly backdrop for mortgage REITs. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, the rate path matters most for Rithm's book value.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: The leveraged S&P 500 fund rose 1.3% Wednesday to $127.44, tracking the market's late recovery with its usual amplified swing. The S&P fell 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the fund's gain reflects the furious afternoon buying rather than a calm day. S&P futures are up about 1.7% into Friday, but leveraged funds cut both ways — a thin half session could magnify any move.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist added 0.9% Wednesday to $47.89, holding firm as the Dow climbed above 50,000 for the first time and banks caught a bid in the late recovery. Financials benefited as the 10-year yield held near 4.85% and the market priced a December hike as near-certain. With futures pointing higher into Friday's half session, the question is whether the Dow can hold its round-number milestone.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony firmed 1.4% Wednesday to $2.21, steadying after Tuesday's 8.8% slide as small miners sold off. China's export curbs and U.S. critical-mineral policy remain the long-term bull case, but the stock still trades on risk appetite day to day. The Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge and recovery set the tone; with futures higher into Friday, the miner could keep steadying if sentiment holds.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy climbed 2.2% Wednesday to $5.69, recovering part of Tuesday's 4.6% slide in the market's late rebound. Nuclear expansion and U.S. uranium buying remain the structural story, but the stock is tied to risk appetite while the Fed's rate path dominates the tape. With oil jumping on Gulf tensions and futures pointing higher, the setup favors a steadier Friday session.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $147.64, down 0.3% on the S&P 500's Wednesday slide, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Dave's account value. The S&P fell as much as 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the estimate reflects the close, not the panic low. With S&P futures up about 1.7%, the next estimate comes after Friday's half session — and a strong open would lift it in step.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 0.5% Wednesday to $323.00 even as the Dow hit 50,000, with oil seesawing and refiners giving back gains. Brent is near $97.30 and WTI $85.85 on Friday after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and a refinery, and mines hit tankers in the strait. Higher crude lifts product prices but squeezes margins, so Valero's direction hinges on how far the supply scare runs.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV nudged up to $28.45 as of Nov 25, a small gain as stocks recovered from intraday lows in the late session. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned the Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge, while its equity holdings joined the afternoon rebound. The next NAV prints after Friday's half session on a thin, holiday-shortened tape for the balanced fund.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws — the VIX spiked to 28.29 Wednesday and the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before recovering. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking toward zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the top-yielding cash parking spot on the board, comfortably ahead of Schwab's SWVXX at 3.79%. With a December hike priced as near-certain, money-fund yields should stay firm into Friday's half session and through the weekend.

weekInBrief.headline: Altria weighs a $30 billion all-cash bid for Imperial Brands
weekInBrief.body: Altria said Thursday it is considering an all-cash offer for London-listed Imperial Brands, valued at about $30 billion before the disclosure, and is talking to an undisclosed third party about carving up part of the business; Japan Tobacco is also reported to be weighing a bid. Imperial shares jumped about 14% to 3,449 pence, and under UK takeover rules Altria has until Dec 24 to make a firm offer or walk away.

weekInBrief.headline: Hackers breach the Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform
weekInBrief.body: Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion was discovered within the past month during a system upgrade and has disrupted work across the platform; Reuters could not establish who the hackers were, the full scope, or whether data was stolen.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump moves to replace Texas judicial nominee opposed by Cornyn
weekInBrief.body: President Trump is moving to replace his judicial nominee for a Dallas-based judgeship after outgoing Senator John Cornyn blocked the pick from advancing. Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley said late Wednesday his panel had received partial nomination paperwork for Steve Fahey, a former prosecutor backed by Cornyn; Trump had previously nominated Justice Department official T. Elliot Gaiser for the seat.

weekInBrief.headline: US famine monitor to halt reporting as funding shortfall hits staff
weekInBrief.body: More than half the field workers at the US government's famine monitor will lose their jobs by the end of the year due to a lack of funding, six people told Reuters, leaving it unable to help fend off famines made more likely by El Nino and aid cuts. Dec 1 termination notices to dozens of employees of the Famine Early Warning Systems Network mean it will be unable to produce its next food security update.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: The Joint Maritime Information Center's Nov 26 advisory put the month's tally at 17 tankers struck in the strait, with four attacks in the latest 96 hours — including the Hong Kong-flagged chemical tanker Kun Peng, hit while transiting outbound off Oman on Nov 26, leaving one seafarer seriously injured. ADNOC also confirmed a Jordanian seafarer missing since a Nov 17 attack on one of its vessels was found dead off Ras Al Khaimah. Iran's Gulf authority blacklisted 26 tugboats for serving ships it says breached its restrictions, a move JMIC warned could hamper rescue and anchorage work, and the IRGC's claims that two tankers hit mines remain unconfirmed. Ashore, a Houthi projectile struck Aramco's 400,000-barrel-a-day Jazan refinery on Nov 26, killing a foreign worker and forcing partial shutdowns. OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday, Nov 29, with delegations signaling output targets will hold steady into the first quarter of 2027.

space.headline: Europa Clipper swings past Earth Dec 3 with all nine instruments on
space.body: NASA announced Nov 25 that Europa Clipper will swing past Earth on Thursday, Dec 3, using the planet's gravity for a propellant-saving boost on its way to Jupiter, coming within about 2,000 miles west of Africa at 3:14 PM EST. All nine science instruments will run during the flyby as a full rehearsal for the Europa campaign, and the spacecraft will reach Jupiter orbit in April 2030.

space.headline: Runaway pulsar escapes the remnant of its own supernova
space.body: Astronomers led by Rohit Dokara at the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy found a rare pulsar that has escaped the debris cloud of the supernova that formed it, spotted by chance while combining two decades of radio surveys. The pulsar is racing away at more than 1,400 km per second — one of the fastest Milky Way pulsars known — and its tail points straight back to the center of the shell it left behind.

space.headline: Google's AI claims a 34-year factoring gap — but nothing is verified yet
space.body: Google Research posted six mathematics papers Nov 25 from its Cogentic system, running on Gemini 4, headlined by a claim to close a 34-year-old gap in integer factoring with the first proven algorithm in the number-field sieve's growth class. The catch: the folder holds only PDFs — no Lean formalization files, no peer review — and the new bound only beats the 1992 result for numbers longer than 60 trillion bits, so the claim is announced, not yet proven.

space.headline: A forgotten organ sheds new light on the origins of the ovary
space.body: University of Geneva researchers found that the cells surrounding and protecting egg cells have two distinct origins, not one — and the second source is the rete ovarii, a small tubular structure first described in 1870 and long dismissed as an embryonic remnant. The finding, published in PNAS and confirmed in early human tissue, opens new avenues for research into fertility, ovarian developmental disorders and gynecological cancers.

apod.title: The Moon Watchers
apod.credit: Marcella Pace — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, Nov. 27, 2026
apod.explanation: On November 24, the Moon rose opposite the setting Sun, big and bright at its full phase. Known to some as a Beaver Moon, November's Full Moon was also near perigee, the closest point in its orbit around Earth, making it one of the biggest and brightest Full Moons — a supermoon — and the first in a series of four consecutive Full Moons near perigee. The next chance to watch a supermoon rise comes when the Cold Moon rises on December 23.
